newsitem.title: UK: Sainsbury details year-end sales figures.
newsitem.headline: Sainsbury details year-end sales figures.

text.p: British supermarket retailer J Sainsbury Plc said on Friday that its sales grew in all its activities on a like-for-like basis in the busy shopping period in the latter part of 1996.

In the eight weeks to January 11 the company's core supermarkets produced an increase in like-for-like sales of 4.4 percent, "and this improvement has been sustained into the new year", it said in a statement.
For the longer 16-week period to January 11, the like-for-like growth was a slightly lower 4.0 percent, and across its Homebase homeware stores sales grew even faster.

Explaining the background to the growth at its supermarkets, where total sales rose by 7.0 percent, Sainsbury said that by adding an Extra Reward Points incentive scheme late last year, only months after the introduction of its loyalty card, it had been able to rebuild sales momentum.
However, the costs of this, in what it called "an extremely competitive" food retailing market, had reduced profitability in the short term.
At its Savacentre hypermarkets, like-for-like sales rose by a sluggish 1.3 percent in the longer 16-week period, while total sales were up 2.8 percent.

"Savacentre's sales growth has reflected the lack of recent store openings, less buoyant clothing sales prior to Christmas and impacts from competitors' store developments," the firm said, adding its next store opening would be in Leeds in March.
During the period, Sainsbury completed the external renaming of its acquired Texas stores, which have been rebranded as Homebase, the company's established home and gardening materials chain.
In performance terms, the original Homebase business made strong progress, with like-for-like sales growth of 7.8 percent, while run-off Texas stores saw a 1.9 percent like-for-like rise.

Sainsbury said it was turning round sales at the stores by rebadging and then later fully converting them to the Homebase format. For 29 Texas stores thus converted, the group reported a 40 percent sales uplift -- "well ahead of appraisal estimates".

However, as the company said it believes conversion is "the key to unlocking the potential of the Texas acquisition", it is speeding up its conversion and adding another 25 stores to its list of projects and as a result is adding 50 million stg to an integration provision set up last March.
While it will convert 40 stores in the current year, this will be increased to 60 in each of the next two years.

In its wholly-owned U.S. supermarket Shaw's, the company is rapidly expanding from its established markets into Connecticut and as a result expects to incur a loss in that state in the current financial year.
The chain's like-for-like sales grew by an average 1.4 percent, though in total terms, with the impact of newly-opened stores, the sales rose by 14.7 percent.
The rapid expansion of Shaw's will reduce its profits for the year, Sainsbury said, but it described its performance in established markets as "very strong".
